title: Chaos rollback simulator and metrics assertion suite for release preflight
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a portable preflight component that simulates realistic upgrade-time failure modes (partial instance failures, sudden KV cache miss storms, p99 latency spikes) and verifies automatic rollback behavior plus metric assertions. The goal is to catch subtle regressions that only surface under degraded cluster conditions and to ensure rollouts against LTS channels trigger safe, deterministic rollback when SLO breaches are detected. This work bundles a chaos scenario composer, a metrics-assertion engine (statistical tests + threshold rules), and an orchestrated dry-run that exercises both smoke and perf eval suites against candidate release images.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable chaos scenario DSL (YAML) that describes node failures, network packet loss, KV-cache purge, and synthetic latency injections
The preflight runner executes the chaos scenario against a staging cluster and reports a pass/fail signal to the release orchestrator within 15 minutes
Metric assertions include KS-test for response-distribution shifts, median/p95/p99 comparisons, and token-per-second throughput checks; all implemented as pluggable assertion modules
Automatic rollback simulation: when a scenario causes SLO breach, system exercises the configured rollback path and validates service recovery in the simulated environment
Integration with existing smoke suite and the golden prompt eval set; failures surface per-prompt diff with example traces for debugging
Runbook snippet and dashboard panels (Grafana) created to explain failure modes and where to look during investigations
Unit and integration tests for the assertion engine with >90% coverage across assertion types
steps: Design DSL: draft YAML schema for chaos scenarios and get design review (link in PRD)
Implement chaos driver adapters (k8s node cordon/kill, network emulation via tc, sidecar latency injection)
Build metrics assertion engine and wire in KS-test and bootstrap A/B comparison util for embeddings / generation quality metrics
Hook preflight runner into release pipeline as an optional gate for LTS channel rollouts
Add dashboard panels and alerts for preflight failures; create an alerting policy that fails the rollout when the gate returns 'fail'
Run dogfood: execute across three representative internal services and one customer-facing sandbox to validate signal quality
Document runbook and add to on-call handbook for release engineers
